direction.premise: A tabletop supersonic-flow instrument, with a luminous compressible-gas chamber and a dark oxide-steel control console.
direction.composition: An unobstructed compressible-flow chamber dominates, with a compact airfoil load bench below the Mach regulator, an experimental pressure-curve plot and selectable retained measurements; portrait phones use a scrollable lower laboratory console.
direction.shapeLanguage: Hard square-cut aluminum geometry, paper-thin graduations, sharp instrument toggles and an uncaged central visualization.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Opaque charcoal-blue oxided metal; brushed mineral wall inclusions; the gas field itself provides dynamic luminous volume. No glassmorphism or decorative gradients over UI components.
direction.paletteLogic: Steel instrument housing and paper-warm brass interaction controls; two restrained signal inks independently encode upper and lower surface pressure, while archived runs appear as hairline dashed traces.
direction.typography: Condensed utility labels with monospaced physical measurements; short Russian action labels remain readable on phones.
direction.signature: A wind-tunnel rig lets the operator physically rotate a pixel-solid airfoil and watch computed pressure loads become lift, drag and pitch moments; four recorded test cards can overlay each surface-pressure curve.
direction.distinction: Where PetriForge is a discrete editable microcosm, SHOCK shows continuous conservation-law fronts and reflective solid boundaries with industrial instrumentation.

architecture.primaryVerb: Tilt the airfoil, run a supersonic flow, read true pressure force and pitching moment, then overlay saved Cp curves to compare stability tendencies.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Rotating the raster-solid profile causes a genuinely different gas-boundary Riemann solution and different pressure traction; saved runs retain coefficients and upper/lower distributions for replay-free comparison.
architecture.spatialRationale: Desktop shows a broad physical chamber and a right instrument console. On portrait phones a compact top bar, live upper canvas and internally scrollable bottom control deck form a header-stage-footer topology, distinct from the desktop split.

comparisons.spatialDifference: PetriForge's tiled Petri grid is replaced by an uncaged fluid image and side instrument console.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Free-hand gas obstacle drawing and physical impulse propagation replace discrete agent rewards.

comparisons.spatialDifference: No paper studio, no painterly cards; industrial short-text control board framing a computational gas tank.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Direct injection and continuous waves replace turn-based drawing.

comparisons.spatialDifference: SHOCK uses a pressure-field instrument bay rather than the source project's discrete object geometry.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Gas impulse injection, boundary drawing and live pressure measurement have distinct controls and physical consequences.

comparisons.spatialDifference: MEAT.EXE fills the viewport with first-person corridors and an environmental combat HUD; SHOCK is a stationary transparent 2D computational gas chamber with laboratory instrumentation.
comparisons.interactionDifference: MEAT.EXE uses continuous exploration and embodied combat; SHOCK uses diaphragm initiation, quantitative sensors, time series and freehand reflective boundaries.

comparisons.spatialDifference: SPACE RUN uses a constructible spacecraft grid surrounded by crew and workshop panels; SHOCK uses one continuous computed pressure chamber and a thin stationary measurement bench.
comparisons.interactionDifference: SPACE RUN's inertial piloting and physical construction differ from SHOCK's numeric Mach inlet, impermeable wall raster, live wave physics and sampled gas instrumentation.

comparisons.spatialDifference: PEREKOS frames two visible combat magicians within a directional projectile battlefield, whereas SHOCK dedicates its main pane to cell-resolved pressure and Mach fields within a fixed measurement chamber.
comparisons.interactionDifference: PEREKOS composes spells and aims magical attacks in real time; SHOCK directly edits impermeable gas-flow obstacles, tunes a boundary Mach number and reads continuously sampled pressure transducers.

production.renderer: Plain Canvas 2D with an offscreen 2D gas raster driven by a JavaScript conservative HLL finite-volume solver; responsive cell resolution.
production.focalAsset: Actual pressure, density and density-gradient fields, with a hand-authored pressure-trace SVG icon.

motion.character: Physical concentric shocks and interference emerge from conservation equations; the UI provides only brief source registration.
motion.action: Immediate impulse and instantaneous solid raster stroke.
motion.anticipation: The selected input tool and canvas crosshair reveal the pending effect.
motion.response: The numerical field reacts during subsequent solver steps and the click adds a minimal source marker.
motion.followThrough: Shock paths refract, diffract and reflect while live time/pressure measurements advance.
motion.interruption: Touch cancellation finishes the active edit and does not leave captured gestures; hiding pauses calculations.
motion.reducedMotion: Animations outside the physical field are removed; physical calculation remains manually pausable.

evidence.expectedChange: A live pressure-load bench appears with computed lift, pressure drag, pitching moment, Cp surface plot and a meaningful Save measurement action.
